1. **Critical error — an eighth open assumption is consumed outside the widened residue set.**

> “CEN-W/CEN-J now carry the displayed hypothesis **(ADM)** … **open at general order** … consumed here”

Yet the claimed residue is only the four tier-1 items plus D-a/D-b/D-c, and §0 asserts:

> “Nothing in tier 2 adds an open lemma”

Those statements are incompatible. Since K3-b consumes ADM at general order, the theorem is additionally conditional on ADM. Calling it “tier-2” does not remove it from the logical hypotheses.

2. **Critical error — other tier-2 conditions are likewise consumed but omitted from the asserted residue union.**

> “TB-CAP dual-accepted, **perimeter-conditional on D-12r**”

> “Theorem A … **conditional on the five §2 flags**”

> “K-FACT … **LITERATURE (LIT-1, conditional grade)**”

The table itself records D-12r at row 8 and ADM at row 17, while its footer nevertheless claims:

> “Residue union over the table … exactly the §0 display”

That union is not exact unless “residue” is artificially restricted to tier 1. Logically, these are consumed conditions outside the requested seven-item set. ADM alone already breaks the headline; D-12r and the five flags reinforce the failure.

3. **Justification gap — the de-anonymized CUT-WD service map is named but not demonstrated.**

> “CUT-WD … ← O-1thr Theorem 1 (= D-14, read locality …) + CU-3 (= F3′ coherent nonempty locus …)”

CUT-WD is described as requiring:

> “the shallow-cut decomposition / exhaustive-exclusive read ownership kernel”

Read locality plus existence/coherence of a nonempty locus does not, from the displayed statements, imply exhaustive and exclusive ownership or the required shallow-decomposition bijection. The note itself concedes that the mapping is “displayed reasoning, not T-6’s own text.” This is load-bearing for K1 and Lemma 3.3, but may be assumed and continued as an explicit gap. The SIB-STEP mapping is comparatively coherent because D-b directly supplies the adapted presentation, depth bound, and read ceiling needed by O-10’s product law.

4. **Justification gap — the oracle-pin rational-function proof is reported, not checkably displayed.**

> “exact agreement … at 44 integer points … with the displayed degree-budget argument”

> “engine numerator/denominator degrees computed per type, ≤ 5; oracle degrees ≤ 7/6 by inspection”

The package does not display the five rational functions, their reduced degrees, the cross-difference polynomials, or the pole checks. If those asserted exact computations and degree bounds are accepted, 44 points are more than sufficient and the argument is mathematically sound. In this fresh-context package, however, the premises of that interpolation argument cannot be verified.

5. **Justification gap — execution and count claims rely on unavailable artifacts.**

> “37/37 PASS + ‘ALL PASS’ summary, exit 0”

> “run 3 … is byte-identical in results”

> “supplement … 10/10 PASS, exit 0”

The repaired arithmetic is internally consistent: V1 8 + V2 6 + T1 23 = 37, and T1’s `(10+1)+(6+1)+(4+1)=23`. Its falsification scope is also now stated correctly: T1 tests the handwritten discriminant proxy and transfers to the real classifier only through conditional K4/K1 inputs. But the actual executions, byte identity, and supplement results are not independently established by the package alone.

6. **Justification gap — the run-history summary remains misleading.**

> “No check ever failed; the defect was the record, not the runs.”

The same section says runs 1 and 2 crashed live before V2/T1. It is defensible to say no emitted assertion reported failure, but the runs themselves did fail. This does not damage the mathematical chain because runs 3–4 supersede them, but the quoted characterization is inaccurate.

The assembly walk remains structurally coherent conditional on all its inputs, and the corrected T1 description avoids the earlier classifier overclaim. Nevertheless, the requested seven-item residue closure fails explicitly at ADM and, under ordinary logical accounting, at further tier-2 conditions.

VERDICT: UNSOUND
